classification.difficultyReason: Systematically pair incident edges at each vertex, including the tetrahedron's hidden edge, and name each angle with its vertex in the middle without duplicating reversed names.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Name all eight angles associated with the figure below.

spec.description: Unmarked quadrilateral ABCD with diagonal DB. Ordinary source blue strokes are rendered black.
spec.mathematics: Edges AB, BC, CD, DA and DB; two rays at A and C, three rays at B and D.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied geometry and labels are visible.

answer.short: $\angle BAD$, $\angle BCD$, $\angle ADC$, $\angle ADB$, $\angle CDB$, $\angle ABC$, $\angle ABD$, $\angle CBD$.
answer.worked:
Keep the vertex letter in the middle and choose each pair of edges meeting there.

At $A$: $\angle BAD$.

At $B$: $\angle ABC$, $\angle ABD$, $\angle CBD$.

At $C$: $\angle BCD$.

At $D$: $\angle ADC$, $\angle ADB$, $\angle CDB$.

This gives $1+3+1+3=8$ angles. Reversing the first and last letters gives an equivalent name.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Name all 12 angles formed at the vertices of the tetrahedron below.

spec.description: Tetrahedron with A above, B left, C below and D right. The hidden edge BD remains dashed. Decorative face shading is omitted; ordinary blue and red source strokes become black, retaining the hidden-edge distinction through dashes.
spec.mathematics: All six edges AB, AC, AD, BC, BD and CD are present. Faces ABC and ACD are visible; BD is behind them.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied vertices and edges only; no angle names are supplied.

answer.short:
At $A$: $\angle BAC$, $\angle CAD$, $\angle DAB$.

At $B$: $\angle ABC$, $\angle CBD$, $\angle DBA$.

At $C$: $\angle ACB$, $\angle BCD$, $\angle DCA$.

At $D$: $\angle ADB$, $\angle BDC$, $\angle CDA$.
answer.worked:
Three edges meet at each vertex. Each pair forms one angle, with that vertex letter in the middle.

At $A$: $\angle BAC$, $\angle CAD$, $\angle DAB$.

At $B$: $\angle ABC$, $\angle CBD$, $\angle DBA$.

At $C$: $\angle ACB$, $\angle BCD$, $\angle DCA$.

At $D$: $\angle ADB$, $\angle BDC$, $\angle CDA$.

There are $4\times3=12$ angles. Reversing the first and last letters gives an equivalent name.
